newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 10.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 10.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING, MARKETING & PUBLIC RELATIONS:

FRANKFURT - The Kirch Group hires Prisma Sport + Media to design a marketing concept for the soccer world championships in 2002 and 2006. Sports marketing firm ISL, which shares the television rights for the championships with Kirch, says the agreement represents a violation of its contract with Kirch. (Horizont)

DREIEICH - Insurance company Axa Direkt says it plans to invest up to 10 million marks ($5.7 million) in a new print and television advertising campaign featuring popular comic book character Asterix. The campaign will be run by Frankfurt agency Ritter & Bee. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Auto rental company Hertz and agency BDDP plan a new campaign for the parking agarage of the Frankfurt Airport. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Regional station NDR says it has formed a new advertising and marketing unit with a focus on event organisation, merchandising and licensing as well as selling ad time. The new subsidiary, NDR Media GmbH, will also serve as a finance and strategy holding company for other NDR units. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Demand for public relations agencies is growing among companies involved in international businness, the German Association of Public Relations Agencies says. A poll of public relations directors at 303 international companies all over the world show that three-quarters said they required the services of independent agencies for company communications. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Schwarzkopf & Henkel Cosmetic Duesseldorf extends its 48-year-old Schauma brand into children's shampoo. The kids' shampoo features the Bubble Joe comic figure and comes in red and blue and in strawberry and cola scents. (Advertising Age)
BONN - German Communications Association BDW says luxury auto maker Audi AG has won its award for excellence in advertising and marketing for 1997. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Deutsche Telekom plans to bring its own digital television decoder box to the market, according to a report in the newspaper Wirtschaftswoche. Telekom is in negotiations with potential manufacturers including Grundig, Sony, Philips and the Sagem Group, according to the newspaper. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Print media will only maintain significance if it avoids falling into the trap of following popularity trends, says the chairman of the advisory board of the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, Hans-Wolfgang Pfeifer. Pfeifer says print media must continue to strengthen the quality of the information they present and their ability to interpret it. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
KITZBUEHEL - Compaq Computer Corp says it plans an autumn introduction of desktop computers powered by a 300 megahertz Pentium II processor from Intel Corp. (Reuter)
MUNICH - Siemens AG and computer networking group 3Com Corp say they have formed an alliance to jointly market and develop voice and data networking products. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Siemens AG says that one of its senior executives had mistakenly told reporters the company was negotiating with Britain's GEC about buying GEC's stake in their GPT telecommunications venture. "There are currently no negotiations with GEC," a Siemens spokesman says(Reuter)

WOLFSBURG - Volkswagen AG says it will shift production of its Golf estate wagon as soon as possible to German carmaker Karmann GmbH due to capacity shortages at its own factories. VW says the total volume of cars to be built by Karmann would depend on demand, which it estimated at about 50,000 vehicles through the end of the contract in mid-1998. (Reuter)

COLOGNE - Retailing group Metro says it expects operating profit this year to exceed last year's 1.062 billion marks. But chairman Klaus Wiegandt told the company's annual general meeting that start-up losses from international operations would total about 100 million marks. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
ZURICH - The editor-in-chief of the SonntagsBlich, Dieter Mittler, is stepping down for personal reasons, publisher Ringier-Verlag says. He had held the position since December 1995. (Reuter)
